instruction: I maintain my work schedule in SimpleNote and track my tasks in Todoist. Every night, I delete the completed tasks from my "Today's Goal" project. Then, I move the maximum number of incomplete tasks from my Inbox to the "Today's Goal" project. The maximum here is assuming I work back-to-back as per my schedule and I find time for the left overs from the current day first. I am busy tonight, please do it for me. Note that the moved tasks must be identical to the original ones.
notes: The instance is a representative placeholder abstraction of runtime data: one completed Today's Goal task (goal-task-done-1, to delete), one leftover incomplete Today's Goal task (goal-task-left-1, untouched but consuming schedule time), and three incomplete Inbox tasks of which two (fits-schedule) fit the remaining schedule and one does not. At runtime the agent instantiates one placeholder per actual record; the selection rule (static fits-schedule facts) is: available minutes = total work minutes of the upcoming work day from the SimpleNote schedule minus minutes of incomplete tasks still in Today's Goal; then take Inbox tasks shortest-first while they fit (hours converted to minutes). 'Moving' a task = todoist.create_task in Today's Goal with identical title/description/due_date/duration/duration_unit/priority, then todoist.delete_task on the Inbox original; completed goal tasks are deleted directly. A single todoist-delete-task action covers both deletion reasons via the unified (removable ?k) predicate (true initially for completed goal tasks, asserted by create-task for copied Inbox tasks); deletion is also gated by tasks-listed so ids are known. Delete-task and create-task carry extra non-API parameters (project/source task) after the API parameters. Apps are domain constants only (not redeclared as problem objects to avoid duplicate-object errors in Fast Downward). supervisor-complete-task takes the task records as parameters so its precondition structurally encodes the goal; no answer is passed since the task is not a question. Usernames are the supervisor's email.
